retention-32.why: 63/64 retention -> 31/32: the child gets LESS, the caller keeps twice as much. core-gas.json only loosens the fraction; this tightens it, which is the direction a forwarding-prediction pre-check and a depth chain's leaf feel.

retention-osaka-256.why: 63/64 -> 255/256 on Osaka, so the pre-Amsterdam arms of the fork-split canaries (valid_until(Osaka)) are mutation-validated too; an Amsterdam-only mutation never selects them.

cold-account-6000.why: COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS 3000 -> 6000, an EIP-2929/EIP-8038-shaped access reprice. This is the `extra_gas` term of calculate_message_call_gas, which a forwarding-prediction slack has to cover.

reservoir-6364.find:
reservoir = gas_meter.state_gas_left
    gas_meter.state_gas_left = StateGas(Uint(0))
    return reservoir
reservoir-6364.replace:
reservoir = StateGas(  # MUTATION
        gas_meter.state_gas_left - (gas_meter.state_gas_left // Uint(64))
    )
    gas_meter.state_gas_left = StateGas(
        gas_meter.state_gas_left - reservoir
    )
    return reservoir
reservoir-6364.why: drain_state_gas_reservoir applies the all-but-one-64th rule to state gas as well, i.e. a later fork 'fixes' the asymmetry its own docstring declares. This is the mutation class #16 exists to catch.

reservoir-half.find:
reservoir = gas_meter.state_gas_left
    gas_meter.state_gas_left = StateGas(Uint(0))
    return reservoir
reservoir-half.replace:
reservoir = StateGas(gas_meter.state_gas_left // Uint(2))  # MUTATION
    gas_meter.state_gas_left = StateGas(
        gas_meter.state_gas_left - reservoir
    )
    return reservoir
reservoir-half.why: the parent keeps half the reservoir back. A coarse version of reservoir-6364, so the pair grades how large a change each archetype can see.
